ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a vertically placed bar magnet, with the upper end of the magnet labeled S and the lower end labeled N; the magnet is located above the center of the coil. The coil is drawn as a horizontally placed perspective parallelogram, and on the front side near the observer there is an arrow, with the arrow pointing to the right, indicating that the induced current in this segment flows to the right. Reasoning: According to the perspective relationship, when looking at the coil from top to bottom, the current on the front side toward the right corresponds to the entire coil current being counterclockwise. According to the right-hand rule, a counterclockwise current produces an upward induced magnetic field at the center of the coil. The lower end of the magnet is the N pole, and the direction of the magnetic field it produces at the coil below is downward. Now the induced magnetic field is upward, indicating that the coil is opposing an “increase in downward magnetic flux.” Only when the N pole of the magnet approaches the coil will the downward magnetic flux passing through the coil increase. Therefore, the magnet should move downward.
